duel.summary: Built the combat spike. Protocol v4 (packages/protocol/src/duel.ts): the batched duel-input message (last 4 frames, 30/s max, validated with the world gate's size, rate, sequence and future-frame limits), frame bundles, probes, practice message, duel create/join options. Rollback core at @pirate-sea-race/simulation/netcode (pure): DuelAuthority (server stepping: first copy wins, late input ignored, 15-frame hold then neutral, a bundle every 3 frames with a snapshot every 2nd), DuelRollback (2 s history, prediction, restore-and-replay with server-applied inputs, per-bundle own-state hash check before restore, gap resync, stable event ids), DuelClock, chooseInputDelay (3 to 8 frames), DuelClientSession (4 ms tick, catch-up cap 4, resync after 30 frames). apps/server: DuelRoom (room 'duel', shared three-layer admission in admission.ts, 2 seats or 1 in practice with an idle/guard dummy, 3 s countdown with RTT probes, delay chosen 30 frames before the end, 10 s reconnect then forfeit), DuelInputGate. packages/test-tools: HeadlessDuelClient (runs the same DuelClientSession), ImpairmentProxy (TCP proxy, WebSocket-frame aware, ordered delays, seeded loss as a 200 ms head-of-line stall), replayRecordedDuel/logFromBundles. apps/web: Create duel / Join duel / Practice on the landing page, Phaser canvas arena (stance, move, state colours, hitbox/hurtbox toggle, one-shot event flashes), duel HUD (health, stamina, clock, round trip / input delay / corrections, result), keyboard with tap latch, dev-only ?rtt=&jitter= socket delay (absent from the production bundle). Tests: netcode, protocol, gate, proxy and web unit tests; integration tests for admission, countdown and delay, throw chord at exact gaps 1/2/3 frames, late input and 250 ms hold, guarding dummy, rejoin and forfeit, and the harness (no impairment and 80 ms/20 ms/1 %: 0 desyncs over 181 hash checks per client, 0 rate-limited drops, 30-34 corrections per 9 s, input delay 3 and 7); e2e duel-practice and duel-online; smoke-build loads netcode from dist and plays a practice duel on the built server. Docs: docs/duel.md netcode section, docs/architecture.md duel section, README. Checks run by me on the final code: npm run typecheck (pass), npm run test:unit (327 pass), npm run test:integration (32 pass), npm run build incl. smoke (pass), full Playwright suite with the JSON reporter (6/6 pass) and check-report (ok). One earlier full Playwright run had out-of-sight fail once (host list polled while the guest coasted past; machine load average 6-13 from other jobs); it passed in the other three full runs. Note: while stopping my own npm run dev I ran 'pkill -f vite', which on this shared VPS may also have stopped another job's vite process.
open_assumptions: Proxy jitter semantics: each direction delays rtt/2 plus a uniform offset in +/- jitter/2 (so 80 ms / 20 ms means round trips of 60-100 ms); loss is per WebSocket frame, retransmitted after a 200 ms RTO with everything behind it held.
Input delay policy: ceil((median RTT / 2 + 2 x IQR of RTT) / 16.7 ms) + 2, clamped to 3-8, from the slower player's countdown probes; a player without samples gets 8.
Documented correction threshold: per client, at most one correction per change of the opponent's applied input plus one per own substituted input, and at most 8 per second.

The practice 'guard' dummy holds back only while player one strikes or while it is in blockstun, so it neither walks out of range nor escapes throws (holding back always walks back in this simulation).
Quitting or staying away 10 s forfeits once the countdown has started; before it, the seat is simply freed.

duel-practice presses J then K back to back (K dispatched without waiting for J's acknowledgement). It reads the frames the client actually tagged: if machine load delivered K more than 2 frames after J, that attempt is checked as the jab the rules make it and pressed again (at most 3 attempts), and the final health accounts for it.
Sea e2e files changed only to use exact: true for the 'Join' button, which 'Join duel' would otherwise also match.
The HUD shows confirmed (server-equal) health, stamina and clock and the room's result; the arena draws the predicted state.

inputs.decisions:
# Decisions: duel-online

From the operator's grill session of 2026-09-24, after slices 1 and 2 (duel core, sea) merged into `main`.

## Decisions

- Duel entry: a standalone Colyseus duel room joined by its own code, plus a practice mode against a server-side dummy. It hosts the same duel simulation object that `MatchRoom` will embed in `encounters-theft` (§14). This keeps the spike isolated from the sea and from reservations, transitions and theft.
- Netcode: §15's server-authoritative prediction and rollback. Clients predict with the shared `stepDuel`; the server sends checkpoints and input acknowledgements, and a mismatch restores the checkpoint and replays. The shared input delay is 3–8 frames, chosen per duel from measured latency. This is the part the spike exists to prove; a plain input-delay model was rejected because its findings would not carry over.
- Wire protocol, revised after design challenge attempt 1 (P1: one input message per frame would hit the unchanged 60-per-second gate cap and drop real presses). Clients send batched, redundant inputs (the last few frames per message, at most 30 messages a second). The server sends one frame bundle per cadence with the inputs it applied, substitutions included, plus a snapshot every second bundle or a hash otherwise. The client rolls back as soon as a confirmed input differs from its prediction; the snapshot is the authority and the desync detector. This is one message type in each direction and one code path to prove.
- The rollback core is a single pure module, `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/netcode`, used by both the browser and the headless harness client (challenge P1: otherwise the harness would prove a reimplementation, not the client the operator plays). It follows the purity rules, with the caller supplying time.
- Evidence must not be trivial: clients compare the hash of their own simulated state at snapshot frames, before restoring anything, and the harness proxy never reorders and turns loss into a head-of-line stall.
- One fullstack lane (`duel`). A lane can't compile against another lane's new types, and the arena, the netcode and the room share new protocol types.
- The spike's exit (§18) is judged by the operator's playtest after the run: guard, punish, throw, simultaneous hit and reconnect must feel credible at §19's latencies. The run delivers the automated evidence (hash agreement and bounded corrections through the impairment harness) and the dev latency setting the playtest needs.
- The sea's density problem (224×208 tiles, 99.2% sea, 10-tile sight radius) is deferred to `encounters-theft`, where sight, speed and travel times can be tuned against real encounters.
- Tests drive input like players do (held keys, short taps, the throw chord with rollover), after world-sea's docking bug passed every check with idealised input.

## Assumptions

- Checkpoints and inputs travel as Colyseus messages over the existing reliable WebSocket; the room's synced Schema state is not used for the duel's frame data. Head-of-line stalls from loss are exactly what the harness measures.
- The duel room reuses the input gate's limits (size, rate, sequence, future frames) with a duel input schema.
- `packages/test-tools` may now depend on `@pirate-sea-race/simulation` (for the replay wrapper and the headless duel client), because this feature owns the lockfile.
- Rates the worker chooses and documents: checkpoint frequency (for example every 6 frames), the input forwarding cadence, and the correction threshold used in the harness test.
- The dummy's behaviour (idle or guarding) is a practice-mode option, not an AI.

## Deferred

- Embedding duels in `MatchRoom`, grapples and challenges, reservations and the 3-second transition from the sea, theft and respawn: `encounters-theft`.
- Haki abilities, fruit kits, art, animation and sound.
- Duel spectating (§6 defers it).
- Tuning the input-delay policy after the playtest (§15 "Tune this policy in the spike"): a follow-up if the playtest asks for it.

concerns.message: Bundles that carry only the inputs the server has already applied mean the shared input delay does nothing to cut rollback for the opponent. The opponent's input takes effect at server frame L'+D. The client hears about it only after the bundle cadence plus the downlink, and by then its displayed frame (tracking the server's) has moved the same distance past L'+D. So rollback depth ≈ bundle wait + downlink, whatever D is. With the §15 wording, 'accepted-input acknowledgements', the server could forward inputs it has received for future frames, marked tentative, through the same rollback path, and then D would absorb part of that latency.
concerns.consequence: In the 80 ms scenario, nearly every change in the opponent's input is rolled back about 4–5 frames, so a 7-frame jab shows up with only 2–3 startup frames left. Raising D in the playtest only adds lag to your own inputs; corrections don't go down. The operator's playtest and any later tuning of the delay policy would then measure the protocol, not rollback over WebSockets. Either decide now whether bundles may forward inputs that are received but not yet applied, or have docs/duel.md record the expected rollback depth, so the playtest verdict is read correctly.

concerns.message: InputGate resets its rate window on server frames (`serverFrame - windowStart >= STEPS_PER_SECOND`, apps/server/src/inputGate.ts:36). stepDuel's frame doesn't advance while the room waits for the second player, during the 3 s countdown, or after the result. Also, `inputAt` and the button latch are world-step behaviour and don't fit per-frame duel inputs.
concerns.consequence: If the duel gate is keyed on the duel frame and clients send inputs or keep-alives before frame 0, the 61st message onward is rate-limited. That breaks the 'zero rate-limited drops' acceptance, or quietly drops the first real presses after the countdown. Key the gate on a room clock that runs from creation, or send nothing before the duel starts. Add a test covering the countdown.

concerns.message: A forfeit (10 s absent, or both clients absent) can't be expressed as a duel result. DuelResult.reason is only ko | double-ko | timeout | overtime, and restoreDuel's REASONS check refuses any other value.
concerns.consequence: If the worker writes a forfeit into DuelState.result, every snapshot after it fails restoreDuel on the clients, so the result screen and the forfeit integration test break. Alternatively, the worker widens the duel types and existing snapshot tests have to change. Keep the forfeit as a room-level result in the protocol's result message, separate from the step's result.

concerns.message: The integration check has 300 s in total, runs files one after another and gives each test 20 s by default. Rounds run in real time: 60 s plus a 3 s countdown. The work adds two harness runs, a 10 s forfeit test, a rejoin test and 1- and 2-frame chord tests, on top of the existing integration tests.
concerns.consequence: If each harness level plays to the result, two levels take about 130 s of wall time before anything else runs. On a slower verifier that is a timeout or a flaky failure. Run a fixed scripted window of about 15 s per level (the result isn't needed for hash, drop or correction evidence), set timeouts per test, and leave margin in the correction threshold. Loss is seeded but timing is real, so counts vary between runs.

concerns.message: The 'zero desyncs' check can pass without checking anything. It compares hashes only for snapshot frames the client has a confirmed state for. After a resync, a stall, or a late start, the client may skip frames, or restore before hashing.
concerns.consequence: A harness that compares few or no snapshots still reports zero desyncs, so the evidence the spike relies on proves nothing. The test should also assert how many hash comparisons were made per client: at least about (scripted frames / snapshot interval) minus a small allowance. It should also assert that the corrections count is non-zero at 80/20/1 %.

concerns.message: A proxy at the WebSocket-message level needs a WebSocket server in test-tools (`ws`, which is only a transitive dependency today). It also has to forward Colyseus's HTTP matchmaking, because the SDK derives the room's WebSocket URL from the same endpoint.
concerns.consequence: This adds a dependency to pin and justify, plus HTTP-forwarding code. If only the WebSocket is proxied, the harness clients may connect to the server directly and measure nothing.

challenge.simpler_alternative: For the harness, build the impairment proxy on raw TCP with `node:net` instead of on WebSocket messages. Each chunk read from one socket is queued per direction, delayed by latency plus seeded jitter, and never reordered. A seeded 'lost' chunk holds everything behind it for an RTO (about 200 ms). This is exactly TCP's head-of-line behaviour. It carries matchmaking HTTP and the WebSocket upgrade without extra code and needs no `ws` dependency. Set noDelay on both sockets so each small Colyseus frame is roughly one chunk. On the netcode side, keep the correction threshold honest: before the real-socket harness exists, run the pure netcode module against a virtual-time channel model in unit tests. There, corrections are reproducible and the threshold can be derived rather than guessed. The real-socket harness then only has to prove zero desyncs and zero drops, with a loose correction bound.
challenge.cheap_experiment: Before writing the room or the browser code, write a roughly 100-line unit test that drives `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/netcode` with caller-supplied time through a virtual channel. Use 40 ms ± 20 ms each way, uplink messages every 2 frames, and bundles every 3 frames. Feed two scripted players whose input changes about every 10 frames. Measure the rollback depth for each change in the opponent's input at D = 3, 5 and 8, in two variants: bundles carrying only applied inputs, and bundles that also forward received future-frame inputs as tentative. If depth under applied-only stays flat as D grows (about 4–5 frames) and the forwarding variant cuts it clearly, settle the bundle contents before the protocol types are fixed. Otherwise keep the decision as written. In the same test, have a gate keyed on the duel frame receive 90 messages over a frozen countdown frame. That confirms or rules out the rate-limit trap in one assertion.

duel.task:
# Task: duel

## Goal

Build the combat spike of §18 stage 1: two browsers fight a 1v1 duel online with the approved duel simulation, through a standalone duel room, with §15's server-authoritative prediction and rollback, and a harness that measures it under simulated latency, jitter and loss. A practice mode against a dummy lets one player try the controls. The spike's exit, "guard, punish, throw, simultaneous hit and reconnect cases are credible online", is judged by the operator's playtest after this run; this task delivers everything that playtest and the automated checks need.

## Context

- Read `docs/spec.md` §6 ("Reservation and transition": countdown, readiness), §7, §8 (controls), §12 (disconnect in a duel), §13 (duel HUD and result), §15 (all of it) and §19 ("Network and performance targets", "Combat determinism").
- Read `docs/duel.md` (the duel simulation: `stepDuel`, snapshots, `restoreDuel`, `replayDuel`, the throw chord window, moveset versioning) and `docs/architecture.md` (rooms, admission, input gate, visibility, tests).
- The duel API is `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/duel` and `@pirate-sea-race/content/moves`. Use it as it is; see Constraints for the one exception.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration`, `npm run build` (ending with `scripts/smoke-build.ts`) and `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`. Playwright's Chromium for `@playwright/test` 1.63.0 is installed and shared read-only; never run `playwright install`.

## Constraints

- Keep the duel rules untouched: no change to what `stepDuel` computes or to the move data. You may add to the duel API (for example, helpers the netcode needs), with unit tests, but any existing test in `packages/simulation/src/duel` or `packages/content/src/moves` must pass unchanged.
- The server is the only authority on hits, health and the result (§15); clients send frame-tagged inputs only, validated with zod in `packages/protocol` like world input, with the same size, rate, sequence and future-frame limits. Bump `PROTOCOL_VERSION`.
- Duel rooms use the same three-layer private admission as matches (code or one-time create token; `onAuth` before any seat; the room's own check), and hold exactly two players, or one in practice mode.
- Keep the sea feature working: all its checks and its four browser scenarios stay green.
- Use existing tooling (Colyseus messages and reconnection, Phaser, zod, Vitest, Playwright). No new runtime dependency unless an existing one cannot do the job; pin exactly and justify it in `docs/architecture.md`.
- Tests must drive input the way players do: keys held through actions, taps shorter than a frame window, the throw chord pressed with ordinary rollover.
- Out of scope: embedding duels in `MatchRoom`, encounters, reservations from the sea, theft, fruit kits, Haki, art and sound.

## Acceptance

- **Duel room** (`apps/server`): a standalone Colyseus room per duel, created by one player with a code the other joins (and a practice variant with a server-side dummy whose behaviour can be switched between idle and guarding). A 3-second countdown starts once both are connected (§6). The room steps `stepDuel` at 60 Hz, applies each player's input for its frame, repeats a player's last input for at most 250 ms and then uses neutral, and never lets late input rewrite a completed frame (§15). It ends the duel with the step's result, which it announces to both.
- **Wire protocol** (see `decisions.md`): clients send **batched, redundant input messages**, each carrying the inputs of the last few frames (for example up to 4, within the 128-byte cap), at no more than 30 messages a second. The server takes each frame's input from the first message that carries it. The existing input gate's limits stay exactly as they are and see zero rate-limited drops in the harness. The server sends one **frame bundle** per cadence (for example every 3 frames) with the inputs it actually applied for each frame since the last bundle, substitutions included, and a full snapshot in every second bundle (the state hash otherwise).
- **Input delay** (§15): the shared input delay is 3 to 8 frames, chosen once per duel from round-trip and jitter measured during the countdown, applied to both players, and shown in the HUD.
- **Rollback core, written once**: a pure module at the subpath `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/netcode` (purity rules apply: the caller supplies time, with no timers and no DOM), unit-tested and loaded from `dist` by `scripts/smoke-build.ts`. It keeps about two seconds of serializable duel states and inputs, predicts both fighters with `stepDuel` (the opponent's last confirmed input repeated), and applies each frame bundle. When a confirmed input differs from what it predicted, it restores the last confirmed state and replays: confirmed frames use the inputs **the server applied** (never the client's own record of what it sent), and later frames use the local and predicted inputs. It counts each correction. The browser client and the headless duel client in `packages/test-tools` both use this module, so the harness proves the code the operator plays.
- **Client clock**: the client's duel frame tracks the server's from the bundles and the measured round-trip: a fixed-step accumulator, a catch-up cap per tick, and a resync from the latest snapshot after a stall or a hidden tab. It does not rely on the display's frame rate. Events that could repeat after a correction (hits, KO) carry stable ids so the view doesn't show them twice.
- **Reconnect** (§12): a player who drops mid-duel gets neutral input after the held-input timeout, can rejoin the same duel within 10 seconds and continue from the authoritative state, and forfeits after 10 seconds absent. An integration test covers rejoining and forfeiting.
- **Arena client**: a Phaser arena scene draws both fighters, their stance and current move with placeholder shapes, with a developer toggle that shows hitboxes and hurtboxes. A duel HUD (§13) shows both health bars, stamina, the round clock, the connection line (round-trip, input delay, corrections) and the result screen. The landing page offers "Create duel", "Join duel" (by code) and "Practice". Controls follow §8: WASD or the arrow keys to move, J light, K heavy, U special one, I special two, Shift dash, and J with K together to throw.
- **Impairment harness** (`packages/test-tools`): a WebSocket proxy that adds latency, jitter and loss the way TCP does. Messages in one direction are never reordered (jitter only delays), and loss becomes a head-of-line stall of about an RTO (for example 200 ms) for everything queued behind it. The random source is seeded. Also a wrapper that runs `replayDuel` on a recorded log.
- **Harness test**: an integration test runs a scripted duel between two headless duel clients through the harness, at no impairment and at the §19 scenario of 80 ms round-trip, 20 ms jitter and 1 % loss. It shows:
  - **zero desyncs**: every client hashes its *own* simulated state at every snapshot frame, before any restore, and compares it with the server's hash;
  - zero rate-limited input drops;

## Acceptance

- **Duel room** (`apps/server`): a standalone Colyseus room per duel, created by one player with a code the other joins (and a practice variant with a server-side dummy whose behaviour can be switched between idle and guarding). A 3-second countdown starts once both are connected (§6). The room steps `stepDuel` at 60 Hz, applies each player's input for its frame, repeats a player's last input for at most 250 ms and then uses neutral, and never lets late input rewrite a completed frame (§15). It ends the duel with the step's result, which it announces to both.
- **Wire protocol** (see `decisions.md`): clients send **batched, redundant input messages**, each carrying the inputs of the last few frames (for example up to 4, within the 128-byte cap), at no more than 30 messages a second. The server takes each frame's input from the first message that carries it. The existing input gate's limits stay exactly as they are and see zero rate-limited drops in the harness. The server sends one **frame bundle** per cadence (for example every 3 frames) with the inputs it actually applied for each frame since the last bundle, substitutions included, and a full snapshot in every second bundle (the state hash otherwise).
- **Input delay** (§15): the shared input delay is 3 to 8 frames, chosen once per duel from round-trip and jitter measured during the countdown, applied to both players, and shown in the HUD.
- **Rollback core, written once**: a pure module at the subpath `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/netcode` (purity rules apply: the caller supplies time, with no timers and no DOM), unit-tested and loaded from `dist` by `scripts/smoke-build.ts`. It keeps about two seconds of serializable duel states and inputs, predicts both fighters with `stepDuel` (the opponent's last confirmed input repeated), and applies each frame bundle. When a confirmed input differs from what it predicted, it restores the last confirmed state and replays: confirmed frames use the inputs **the server applied** (never the client's own record of what it sent), and later frames use the local and predicted inputs. It counts each correction. The browser client and the headless duel client in `packages/test-tools` both use this module, so the harness proves the code the operator plays.

It does not rely on the display's frame rate. Events that could repeat after a correction (hits, KO) carry stable ids so the view doesn't show them twice.

Messages in one direction are never reordered (jitter only delays), and loss becomes a head-of-line stall of about an RTO (for example 200 ms) for everything queued behind it. The random source is seeded. Also a wrapper that runs `replayDuel` on a recorded log.
- **Harness test**: an integration test runs a scripted duel between two headless duel clients through the harness, at no impairment and at the §19 scenario of 80 ms round-trip, 20 ms jitter and 1 % loss. It shows:

# Decisions: duel-online

From the operator's grill session of 2026-09-24, after slices 1 and 2 (duel core, sea) merged into `main`.

## Decisions

- Duel entry: a standalone Colyseus duel room joined by its own code, plus a practice mode against a server-side dummy. It hosts the same duel simulation object that `MatchRoom` will embed in `encounters-theft` (§14). This keeps the spike isolated from the sea and from reservations, transitions and theft.
- Netcode: §15's server-authoritative prediction and rollback. Clients predict with the shared `stepDuel`; the server sends checkpoints and input acknowledgements, and a mismatch restores the checkpoint and replays. The shared input delay is 3–8 frames, chosen per duel from measured latency. This is the part the spike exists to prove; a plain input-delay model was rejected because its findings would not carry over.
- Wire protocol, revised after design challenge attempt 1 (P1: one input message per frame would hit the unchanged 60-per-second gate cap and drop real presses). Clients send batched, redundant inputs (the last few frames per message, at most 30 messages a second). The server sends one frame bundle per cadence with the inputs it applied, substitutions included, plus a snapshot every second bundle or a hash otherwise. The client rolls back as soon as a confirmed input differs from its prediction; the snapshot is the authority and the desync detector. This is one message type in each direction and one code path to prove.
- The rollback core is a single pure module, `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/netcode`, used by both the browser and the headless harness client (challenge P1: otherwise the harness would prove a reimplementation, not the client the operator plays). It follows the purity rules, with the caller supplying time.
- Evidence must not be trivial: clients compare the hash of their own simulated state at snapshot frames, before restoring anything, and the harness proxy never reorders and turns loss into a head-of-line stall.
- One fullstack lane (`duel`). A lane can't compile against another lane's new types, and the arena, the netcode and the room share new protocol types.
- The spike's exit (§18) is judged by the operator's playtest after the run: guard, punish, throw, simultaneous hit and reconnect must feel credible at §19's latencies. The run delivers the automated evidence (hash agreement and bounded corrections through the impairment harness) and the dev latency setting the playtest needs.
- The sea's density problem (224×208 tiles, 99.2% sea, 10-tile sight radius) is deferred to `encounters-theft`, where sight, speed and travel times can be tuned against real encounters.
- Tests drive input like players do (held keys, short taps, the throw chord with rollover), after world-sea's docking bug passed every check with idealised input.

## Assumptions

- Checkpoints and inputs travel as Colyseus messages over the existing reliable WebSocket; the room's synced Schema state is not used for the duel's frame data. Head-of-line stalls from loss are exactly what the harness measures.
- The duel room reuses the input gate's limits (size, rate, sequence, future frames) with a duel input schema.
- `packages/test-tools` may now depend on `@pirate-sea-race/simulation` (for the replay wrapper and the headless duel client), because this feature owns the lockfile.
- Rates the worker chooses and documents: checkpoint frequency (for example every 6 frames), the input forwarding cadence, and the correction threshold used in the harness test.
- The dummy's behaviour (idle or guarding) is a practice-mode option, not an AI.

## Deferred

- Embedding duels in `MatchRoom`, grapples and challenges, reservations and the 3-second transition from the sea, theft and respawn: `encounters-theft`.
- Haki abilities, fruit kits, art, animation and sound.
- Duel spectating (§6 defers it).
- Tuning the input-delay policy after the playtest (§15 "Tune this policy in the spike"): a follow-up if the playtest asks for it.

completion.summary: Built the combat spike. Protocol v4 (packages/protocol/src/duel.ts): the batched duel-input message (last 4 frames, 30/s max, validated with the world gate's size, rate, sequence and future-frame limits), frame bundles, probes, practice message, duel create/join options. Rollback core at @pirate-sea-race/simulation/netcode (pure): DuelAuthority (server stepping: first copy wins, late input ignored, 15-frame hold then neutral, a bundle every 3 frames with a snapshot every 2nd), DuelRollback (2 s history, prediction, restore-and-replay with server-applied inputs, per-bundle own-state hash check before restore, gap resync, stable event ids), DuelClock, chooseInputDelay (3 to 8 frames), DuelClientSession (4 ms tick, catch-up cap 4, resync after 30 frames). apps/server: DuelRoom (room 'duel', shared three-layer admission in admission.ts, 2 seats or 1 in practice with an idle/guard dummy, 3 s countdown with RTT probes, delay chosen 30 frames before the end, 10 s reconnect then forfeit), DuelInputGate. packages/test-tools: HeadlessDuelClient (runs the same DuelClientSession), ImpairmentProxy (TCP proxy, WebSocket-frame aware, ordered delays, seeded loss as a 200 ms head-of-line stall), replayRecordedDuel/logFromBundles. apps/web: Create duel / Join duel / Practice on the landing page, Phaser canvas arena (stance, move, state colours, hitbox/hurtbox toggle, one-shot event flashes), duel HUD (health, stamina, clock, round trip / input delay / corrections, result), keyboard with tap latch, dev-only ?rtt=&jitter= socket delay (absent from the production bundle). Tests: netcode, protocol, gate, proxy and web unit tests; integration tests for admission, countdown and delay, throw chord at exact gaps 1/2/3 frames, late input and 250 ms hold, guarding dummy, rejoin and forfeit, and the harness (no impairment and 80 ms/20 ms/1 %: 0 desyncs over 181 hash checks per client, 0 rate-limited drops, 30-34 corrections per 9 s, input delay 3 and 7); e2e duel-practice and duel-online; smoke-build loads netcode from dist and plays a practice duel on the built server. Docs: docs/duel.md netcode section, docs/architecture.md duel section, README. Checks run by me on the final code: npm run typecheck (pass), npm run test:unit (327 pass), npm run test:integration (32 pass), npm run build incl. smoke (pass), full Playwright suite with the JSON reporter (6/6 pass) and check-report (ok). One earlier full Playwright run had out-of-sight fail once (host list polled while the guest coasted past; machine load average 6-13 from other jobs); it passed in the other three full runs. Note: while stopping my own npm run dev I ran 'pkill -f vite', which on this shared VPS may also have stopped another job's vite process.
open_assumptions: Proxy jitter semantics: each direction delays rtt/2 plus a uniform offset in +/- jitter/2 (so 80 ms / 20 ms means round trips of 60-100 ms); loss is per WebSocket frame, retransmitted after a 200 ms RTO with everything behind it held.
Input delay policy: ceil((median RTT / 2 + 2 x IQR of RTT) / 16.7 ms) + 2, clamped to 3-8, from the slower player's countdown probes; a player without samples gets 8.
Documented correction threshold: per client, at most one correction per change of the opponent's applied input plus one per own substituted input, and at most 8 per second.

The practice 'guard' dummy holds back only while player one strikes or while it is in blockstun, so it neither walks out of range nor escapes throws (holding back always walks back in this simulation).
Quitting or staying away 10 s forfeits once the countdown has started; before it, the seat is simply freed.

duel-practice presses J then K back to back (K dispatched without waiting for J's acknowledgement). It reads the frames the client actually tagged: if machine load delivered K more than 2 frames after J, that attempt is checked as the jab the rules make it and pressed again (at most 3 attempts), and the final health accounts for it.
Sea e2e files changed only to use exact: true for the 'Join' button, which 'Join duel' would otherwise also match.
The HUD shows confirmed (server-equal) health, stamina and clock and the room's result; the arena draws the predicted state.
untested: Hidden-tab and stall resync in a real browser (unit-tested with a fake clock only).

The dev latency setting end to end: only its query parsing is unit-tested and its absence from the production bundle is checked; I verified it once by hand under npm run dev (round trip 12 ms without it, 117 ms with ?rtt=80&jitter=20).
Reconnect from a browser page (the SDK's automatic reconnect is covered only with the headless client through the proxy).
The other section 19 combinations (30/150 ms, 50 ms jitter, 3 % loss); the harness runs no impairment and 80 ms / 20 ms / 1 % only.
Whether guard, punish, throw, simultaneous hits and reconnect feel credible at latency (the operator's playtest).
completion.verify_yourself: That the chosen input delay feels right at your real latencies: it is picked from probes during the countdown, when the joining page is still booting the arena, so a busy client inflates it (on this loaded VPS a local duel sometimes chose 6 frames at a ~10 ms round trip).
